value.body: A polytechnic diploma is a technician-level qualification in engineering and applied fields — civil, mechanical, electrical, electronics, computer and more. It normally takes 3 years after Class 10; Class 12 (Science or vocational) and ITI pass students can usually join directly in the second year. Programmes are AICTE-approved and diplomas are awarded by state technical boards.

items.label: Course length
items.note: About 2 years with lateral entry after Class 12 or ITI, in many states

items.label: Diploma (engineering) approved intake
items.note: About half of seats reported vacant
items.source: AICTE data, via Avanti Fellows analysis (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Through state-run admissions: entrance tests such as JEECUP (Uttar Pradesh) or POLYCET (Telangana, Andhra Pradesh), or merit-based counselling in other states. Class 12 Science or vocational students — and ITI pass-outs — apply for direct second-year (lateral) admission where the state allows it.

value.title: At a glance
items: Diploma holders can enter B.Tech/B.E. in the second year through state lateral-entry tests (for example ECET or LEET).
A diploma meets the qualification for junior engineer (JE) posts in many government departments, through exams such as SSC JE.
For Class 12 Science students, a diploma followed by lateral-entry B.Tech takes about a year longer than a direct B.Tech, with an earlier exit point into work.
Quality, seat-fill and placements vary widely between institutes.

value.title: Enrolment in technical / polytechnic institutes
value.note: Responding polytechnics: 3,599 (2021-22), 3,530 (2022-23), 4,209 (2023-24), so coverage differs by year. Stand-alone technical/polytechnic institutes only; diplomas run by universities are not included.
value.source: AISHE 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24, stand-alone institutions section (Ministry of Education)
